Definition: Understandability refers to how easily developers can comprehend and maintain the test code.

Task: Improve the understandability of the test `TestPaxChronology_test_LocalDate_from_PaxDate.java` (path:- /Users/tenghaha/Projects/New_Agent_understandability_improvement/data/original/threeten-extra/manual/testcases/TestPaxChronology/TestPaxChronology_test_LocalDate_from_PaxDate.java). The refactored code must be syntactically correct and compilable against the provided CUT signatures. Do not alter the runtime behaviour of the original test: the same methods must be called with the same arguments and produce the same expected outcomes.

This test only exercises `data_samples()` and `test_LocalDate_from_PaxDate`; the other ~10 data methods and most imports are dead code. I'll write a focused, readable version. Let me create it.The original relied on default-package + package-private `PaxDate`, which doesn't resolve. I'll add the package declaration so `PaxDate` resolves.Compiles successfully. The refactored test preserves the original behavior — same `LocalDate.from(pax)` call against the same 52 Pax/ISO date pairs — while improving understandability: dropped the ~10 unused data methods and dozens of unused imports, added explanatory Javadoc, grouped the samples by calendar feature (epoch boundary, leap years, century rules, BCE years) with comments, and gave the test/provider/parameters descriptive names. (I added a `package org.threeten.extra.chrono;` declaration so the package-private `PaxDate` resolves at compile time.)
